Steel Industry in China Hit by Deepening Credit Freeze, Output Slashed

BEIJING, June 25—China’s steel sector is facing escalating turmoil as a worsening credit freeze leaves mills unable to refinance debts or secure operating capital, industry groups and analysts said Tuesday. The crisis has already forced dozens of steel producers to halt or sharply curtail production, with market participants warning of further shutdowns in the coming weeks.

The China Steel Association reported that steel output in key provinces, including Hebei and Jiangsu, fell by 18% in the past month, the steepest decline since 2015. “The liquidity crunch is unprecedented. Many medium and small mills are simply unable to roll over loans or access new credit,” said Zhang Wei, a spokesperson for the association. “We are seeing inventories piling up and cash flows drying up rapidly.”

At several major plants, workers have been placed on unpaid leave or temporary furloughs, according to the National Steel Workers Union. “We are very worried about job security. Some of our members haven’t received full wages in two months,” said union official Liu Jun. “The government needs to step in urgently.”

Analysts at Zhonghua Securities estimate that at least 40 steel companies are at risk of defaulting on bond payments within the next quarter. Domestic steel prices have tumbled 12% since May, intensifying the pressure on already-strained balance sheets.

Regulators have yet to announce any sector-specific relief measures. “Unless access to credit is restored soon, the risk of large-scale bankruptcies is real,” said Lin Tao, a senior industry analyst. The situation remains fluid.
